memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Meanwhile, Abimelek had come to him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his personal adviser and Phicol the commander of his forces. Isaac asked them, 'Why have you come to me, since you were hostile to me and sent me away?' They answered, 'We saw clearly that the LORD was with you; so we said, "There ought to be a sworn agreement between us"—between us and you. Let us make a treaty with you that you will do us no harm, just as we did not harm you but always treated you well and sent you away peacefully. And now you are blessed by the LORD.' Isaac then made a feast for them, and they ate and drank. Early the next morning the men swore an oath to each other. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they went away peacefully." - Gen 26:26-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The very people who had pushed Isaac away now come seeking peace with him. And their reason is striking: "We saw clearly that the LORD was with you." Isaac's peaceable, God-blessed life had become a testimony that even his opponents could not ignore. They wanted to be on good terms with a man they could tell God was with.

This is the power of a faithful life. Isaac did not preach a sermon or force his beliefs on them. He simply lived in such a way — patient under mistreatment, blessed by God, choosing peace over conflict — that others recognised God's hand on him. His character spoke louder than words.

Jesus said, "Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven" (Matt 5:16). People are watching how we handle unfairness, success, and conflict. When they see grace, patience, and blessing in us, they catch a glimpse of the God we serve.

And notice Isaac's grace: he does not hold a grudge. He makes a feast for these former enemies and sends them away in peace. What a picture of the reconciling heart God gives His people. May our lives, like Isaac's, make others say, "Surely the Lord is with them."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Would those around me say, "The Lord is with that person"?
2. How do I handle former conflicts — with grudges or with grace?
3. What is my life "preaching" to those who watch me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let my life be a testimony that You are with me. Give me grace to make peace even with those who once opposed me, so others may glorify You. Amen.
